correctness.rationale: The graph is defined from the six nonzero quadratic residues modulo thirteen; a disconnected induced triple spans at most one edge. The complete enumeration gives 143 facets, 7,878 nonempty faces and 50,076 face-poset covers. The packaged verifier creates 3,936 face/coface pairs, verifies all reverse-match Hasse orientations by a complete 7,878-vertex topological sort, and leaves one 0-cell, three 7-cells and two 8-cells. Exact oriented integer gradient-path eliminations give the two columns (-1,-1,1), so the remaining 3-by-2 cellular boundary is primitive of rank one. The 7-skeleton is a wedge of three 7-spheres; for attaching 8-cells, the degree vectors classify maps into this skeleton because pi_7(wedge^3 S^7)=Z^3. A unimodular change of basis and cancellation yield the integral homotopy type two S^7 wedge one S^8. The separate Alexander-dual enumeration has augmented face counts (1,13,78,143,78) and boundary ranks (12,66,76) independently over six primes, corroborating Betti ranks only; finitely many fields cannot prove integral torsion-freeness. Both packaged scripts reproduced their reference outputs.

value.rationale: The order-thirteen quadratic-residue Paley graph is a canonical self-complementary strongly regular graph with a natural ordinary three-cut invariant, not an arbitrary sampled subgraph or chosen parameter slice. Its full integral homotopy type is mixed-dimensional despite a pure 9-dimensional face structure, giving an explicit obstruction to shellability outside common pure-sphere statements. The primitive integer Morse differential establishes an actual homotopy decomposition, beyond numerical Betti counts, finite-field tests or known symmetric-neighborhood data. Mathematical scope is deliberately one exact natural finite case; no unsound family extrapolation is claimed.
